i wonder about the distinction between the two words. if i go to a library to get books for school, can i use the word to order things to me in a certain way? because it seems like it is similar to the word order (in english there are also ways of ordering things) in order to get the book. in the book there is the word arrangement. can someone explain this to me.

is it correct to say that a book is a collection of books and the arrangement of the books within the book is a result of the author’s mind, the writer’s thoughts and that of the people who wrote the book? or does it mean that the words are not written but are still in the book?

is the arrangement of the books in the book the author’s mind, writer’s thoughts and the words of the person who wrote the book, or is it the book itself?

it seems to me that the second interpretation is more plausible. the books are a result of the author’s and the writer’s thoughts; so it’s more reasonable to say that the arrangement of the books in the book belongs to the author, to the writer and to the readers
